title: KV slab multiplexing + latency-aware gang eviction for multi-GPU KV cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On large tensor/pipeline parallel topologies we observe suboptimal utilization of GPU memory for KV caches: cold tails occupy contiguous slabs while hot prefixes cause repeated remote fetches, creating latency spikes for small tail-latency SLOs. Existing slab striping and static shard placement lead to cross-rank contention when bursts hit the same key hotset.

Proposal: Implement a slab multiplexing + latency-aware gang eviction scheme that: 1) slices KV slabs into variable "slablets" that can be colocated opportunistically across ranks (not purely round-robin); 2) introduces a light-weight remap table per GPU to map slablet -> owning-rank and to track a recency/heat score; 3) uses a gang-eviction policy that evicts groups of slablets together when they are co-located and producing tail spikes, favoring eviction of cold co-resident slabs to free space fast without fragmenting hot prefixes; 4) supports asymmetric light-weight replication for extremely hot keys (1-2 copies) to avoid remote fetch during short-lived spikes; 5) coordinates with the serving runtime's gang scheduler so tensor-parallel and pipeline-parallel ranks that execute together are considered a single eviction domain to reduce cross-domain thrash.

Design details:
- Slablet size: adaptive, default 64KB to 256KB depending on model KV footprint and observed average token cache entry size.
- Remap table: compact fixed-size hash with linear probing; entries store slablet id, owning-rank id, heat-epoch counter, and a small LRU hint. Implemented as a per-GPU memory-mapped structure with atomic updates.
- Heat scoring: exponential decay counters per slablet updated on access; thresholds determine prefetch vs replicate decisions.
- Gang eviction: when memory pressure crosses soft-threshold, coordinator ranks identify co-located slablet groups (slablets that belong to same model prefix or same mapped region) and evict whole groups prioritizing minimal impact on recent hits.
- Asymmetric replication: replicate only top-N hottest slablets for short epochs, revoke replicas when heat decays. Replication uses cheap RDMA/copy between GPUs in same node or cross-node via GPUDirect where available.
- Local spill and prioritized prefetch: evicted slablets spill to efficient host-resident slab store; prefetch budgets are token-aware and constrained by latency SLOs.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Complexity: introduces remap metadata and cross-rank coordination which increases control-path complexity. We'll mitigate with strict limits on table size and a fallback to current striping behavior if coordinator fails.
- Network cost: replication introduces extra GPU-GPU traffic; to limit cost we cap replication rate and prefer intra-node replicas.
- Fragmentation: slablet slicing may increase fragmentation; compaction task scheduled during low load windows.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Reduce 99th-percentile token latency for mixed traffic (30% small-chat, 70% long generation) by >= 12% compared to baseline.
- Reduce remote fetch rate (cross-rank KV misses) by >= 20% for attack/spike scenarios.
- No >5% regression in average throughput for steady-state workloads.
- Memory efficiency: achieve >= 15% reduction in reserved GPU KV memory for equivalent hit-rate.

Compatibility: Works with existing model shard placement. No model graph changes required. Exposed via runtime config flags: kv.slablet.enabled, kv.replicate.hot.enabled, kv.eviction.gang_size.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype remap table and slablet allocator (branch: feature/kv-slablet).
2) Add heat counters and local eviction logic; benchmark on single-node 4xA100.
3) Implement gang discovery and eviction coordinator for pipeline+tensor co-scheduling.
4) Add replication and RDMA paths with opt-in flag.
5) Integration tests, perf runs, then staged rollout on canary fleet.

Rollout and rollback:
- Rollout: enable slablet allocator as opt-in for selected workloads, then broaden to canary fleet with telemetry comparing remote fetch rate and tail latency.
- Rollback: config toggle to disable slablet remap and fall back to original slab striping; automatic rollback if 99p latency increases >10% or remote fetch increases >25% in 1h window.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for remap table concurrency and eviction atomicity.
- Microbenchmarks for remap lookup cost and memory overhead.
- System tests simulating hotkey spikes, mixed-length generations, and node failures.
- End-to-end perf on 2-node and 8-node topologies with mixed TP/PP settings.

Observability: new metrics: kv_slablet_hits, kv_slablet_misses, kv_slablet_replica_count, kv_gang_evictions, kv_remote_fetch_rate, kv_remap_load_factor. Dashboards and alerts for remote_fetch_rate and 99p token latency.

Docs and operator controls: console toggles for slablet sizing and replication caps; CLI tooling to dump remap table for debugging.

Dependencies: requires micro-batching scheduler hooks (ENG-700212) and node RDMA enablement (INF-1210).

2026-03-01: Design review with runtime and infra teams. Decided to scope replication to intra-node first; cross-node replication behind feature flag. Action: update design doc with RDMA fallback. - Aisha
2026-03-05: Initial gang eviction algorithm implemented. Local correctness tests pass; still need to tune heat decay constants to avoid thrashing on bursty chat workloads. - Marco

2026-03-10: Perf run on 4xA100 single node: 99p token latency down 13% in mixed workload; remote fetch rate down 27% with replication enabled (intra-node). Throughput stable. Added compaction job scheduled at 03:00 UTC. - Marco
2026-03-13: Security review: no direct customer data exposure in remap metadata; however need to ensure memzero on eviction to meet compliance. Security notes added. - Priya (Security)
2026-03-14: Preparing canary rollout. Creating PR and release train entries. - Aisha
